observation.visible_scene: A hazy coniferous forest interior. A large, moss-and-lichen-covered tree trunk dominates the left-center foreground; behind it stand several vertical trunks fading into bright mist, with visible shafts of sunlight (god rays) slanting down from the upper right. The right side and forest floor are covered in ferns and mossy fallen logs. A fixed text overlay 'NORTHEY PHOTOGRAPHY' sits in the bottom-left corner throughout (a watermark, not part of the scene).
visible_changes: A slow, steady camera drift/pan: across the segment the foreground trunk slides leftward in the frame more than the background trunks do, indicating a gentle rightward pan with parallax rather than any object moving on its own.
The mist and sunbeam brightness shimmer subtly from frame to frame, with the central background glow appearing to pulse slightly in intensity.
No people, animals, or moving objects enter the frame; the ferns and trunks themselves show no clear independent motion.
The watermark overlay remains pixel-locked in the bottom-left corner, confirming it is a static graphic.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the pan continues or reverses after t=3.33s, and what preceded t=0s, is not shown.
The cause of the mist and light variation (real atmospheric change vs. exposure/compression flicker) cannot be determined from the frames alone.
uncertain_details: The exact direction and speed of the camera pan are inferred from small relative shifts; the scene is nearly static and the motion is very slow.
Any faint sway of fern fronds (e.g., from wind) is not clearly distinguishable from the camera drift or compression noise.

NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
